title: Performance Campaign — perf-trial-20260906-0303
summary: Wave 1 (merged to main): deals 107ms -> 0.26ms, page weight -75%, test suite 12.25s -> 2.6s, projection 17MB -> 15.6MB. Wave 2 so far: deals cache now invalidates immediately when the projection DB changes on disk, and the projection rebuild dropped from ~1.9s to 0.24s (8x) via prepared-statement reuse + a single transaction - output verified byte-identical. Scale-resilience lane still running.

improvements.title: Memoized /api/deals (per-retailer TTL cache)
improvements.what: The deal computation (90-day observation query + calculateSales + calculateOngoingSales + sorting) is now computed once per retailer and reused for 5 minutes (DEALS_CACHE_TTL_MS env, 0 disables). Filter, limit, and signed-in tier ordering still apply per request; cached deal objects are never mutated (tier path copies).
improvements.beforeAfter: p50 107.4ms -> 0.26ms warm (~400x); cold cache-fill request unchanged ~150ms. 8-way burst was 8.5 req/s serialized - now bounded by JSON output only.
improvements.tradeoffs: Deal feed can be up to 5 minutes staler than a full recompute (in practice prices only change on the nightly rebuild, so real staleness is unchanged). Memory measured with forced GC: server boots at ~63MB RSS; with all 6 retailer deal universes cached, live heap is only ~8MB total - RSS may climb to ~160MB transiently during a compute, but the uncached path had the identical spike on EVERY request. DEALS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0 restores exact old behavior.
improvements.verified: 6 new unit tests (TTL, per-retailer keys, filter/limit, tier no-mutation) + full suite 854 pass / 0 fail; bench-server before/after

improvements.title: Test suite: 12.25s -> 2.78s
improvements.what: Two seams added so tests stop paying production waiting costs: (1) MobileFoodstuffsClient retry backoff is injectable (retryBackoffMs; production default 3000ms unchanged) - two retry-semantics tests were sleeping through real 3s+6s backoffs. (2) Auth takes options.scryptOptions (production N=16384 unchanged); the test harness defaults to N=256, keeping register/verify self-consistent per instance.
improvements.beforeAfter: npm test 12.25s -> 2.78s (4.4x). Foodstuffs adapter file 12.3s -> 0.06s; private-api 2.56s -> 0.40s; auth 1.3s -> 0.13s; security ~1.9s -> 0.30s.
improvements.tradeoffs: None at runtime: production retry count/pacing and scrypt cost are byte-identical; only tests inject cheaper values. Slight risk that a future test asserting production-cost timing would need an explicit override.
improvements.verified: Full suite 854 pass / 0 fail at every step; per-suite timings re-measured

improvements.title: Projection DB: 17MB -> 15.6MB and faster search
improvements.what: Three schema-level cuts to the rebuildable projection: (1) removed creation of the documented-dead deal_signals and product_matches tables; (2) removed the redundant idx_or_offer_key by reordering the offer_revisions UNIQUE constraint to (offer_key, observed_at, rev_hash) - same uniqueness, but the index now also serves offer lookups and ordering (EXPLAIN: no temp b-tree); (3) rebuild now sets PRAGMA page_size=8192 before WAL.
improvements.beforeAfter: DB size 17MB -> 15.6MB (-8%). GET /api/products?search= p50 4.4ms -> 0.73ms (larger pages, shallower index). build-db time unchanged (~1.9s).
improvements.tradeoffs: Schema edit relies on the projection being rebuildable (every rebuild builds a fresh temp DB - verified no code path re-applies migrations to an existing DB). Any external tool that reads deal_signals/product_matches or expects 4KB pages would break; none exist in this repo. 8KB pages cost slightly more RAM per cached page.
improvements.verified: 116 sqlite tests pass (schema test now asserts dead tables stay deleted); EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN checks; full suite 854/0; server re-bench

improvements.title: Web interface: wire weight -75%, zero-refetch view switches
improvements.what: Server side (by the web subagent lane, reviewed + merged by coordinator): static files served with brotli/gzip negotiation (variants compressed once per file version and cached in ~104KB of RAM), weak ETags with 304 revalidation (warm page reload transfers 0 bytes), memory-cached file reads keyed by mtime; JSON API responses gzip-compressed when over 1KB. Frontend: GET responses cached 30s with shared in-flight requests and full invalidation on any mutation, so switching views no longer refetches identical data; removed a DOM-allocating esc() helper that was also double-escaping ampersands (display bug fix - the DOM helper already escapes via text nodes).
improvements.beforeAfter: Cold SPA page load: 66,962 B -> 17,331 B brotli (-75%), 20,122 B gzip (-69%); warm reload = 0 B (13 x 304). GET /api/products?limit=120: 39,869 B -> 5,622 B (-86%). Loopback latency unchanged within noise.
improvements.tradeoffs: gzipSync runs on the event loop (~0.2ms per 40KB API response) - fine vs the 107ms deals win it sits on top of; brotli's heavier compression is paid once per file version, not per request. Static assets keep max-age=3600 (no content hashes exist in a no-build repo, so HTML stays no-cache). API GET cache means up to 30s staleness, but every mutation clears it. Reviewed for security: the removed esc() was redundant (createTextNode escaping) and no innerHTML path takes unescaped product data.
improvements.verified: 38 new/updated compression+cache tests pass; 15 original static tests pass against the real implementation; full suite 877 pass / 0 fail on the merged branch; wire sizes measured with curl --compressed

improvements.title: Wave 2: deals cache invalidates on projection change
improvements.area: server / correctness of the wave-1 perf win
improvements.what: createAppServer passes a dbSignature probe (projection DB file mtime, ~microseconds per request) into the public handlers; a changed signature drops the deals cache immediately instead of waiting out the 5-minute TTL.
improvements.beforeAfter: Worst-case stale-after-rebuild: up to 5 min -> immediate (still bounded by the read-only connection serving the old inode until server restart).
improvements.tradeoffs: One statSync per /api/deals request (~10 microseconds). Absent probe = TTL-only, so library callers keep old behavior.
improvements.verified: 8 deals-cache unit tests (signature change recomputes, stable signature caches, absent probe = TTL-only) + npm run check

improvements.title: Wave 2: projection rebuild ~1.9s -> 0.24s (8x)
improvements.what: Profiling showed ~87% of rebuild time in per-record SQL statement compiles (~100k per rebuild) and per-statement autocommit journaling. The insert phase now prepares its 13 statements once, runs in a single transaction, and sets synchronous=OFF on the throwaway temp connection only. Rowid read from the INSERT result instead of a follow-up query.
improvements.beforeAfter: 18,726-record archive: 1.88s -> 0.24s. 35,039-record NW archive: 3.87s -> 0.45s. Output byte-identical (only _meta.built_at differs, which varies run to run).
improvements.tradeoffs: synchronous=OFF means a crash mid-rebuild could corrupt the temp DB - it was always discarded unpublished, so nothing real is exposed. The authoritative JSONL writer fsync semantics are untouched.
improvements.verified: Content-identity tool (rows, integer aggregates, schema, meta) says IDENTICAL vs a pre-change build; 116 sqlite tests + full suite 906 pass / 0 fail; caught in review: the identity tool initially lived in test/ where the runner executes it and fails - moved to tools/.

stops: Library JSONL load: 340ms / 216MB RSS on the 12MB archive (672ms / 540MB on the 22MB breadth archive). No consumer is on this path today (the app server uses SQLite and never holds the archive; collectors are network-bound; the old Workbench grocery project no longer exists). Speeding it up would mean weakening per-line hash verification - a data-integrity tradeoff for zero user-visible gain.
Fuzzy product matching: 0.17s on fresh DBs, capped at 1000 candidates - already fast.
local-archive-runner tests (~1.8s of the 2.8s suite): they exist to run the real shell script; faking the shell would weaken the guarantee.
Server memory: 63MB RSS at boot, ~8MB live heap even with all six retailer deal caches populated (measured with forced GC). No leak, nothing to reclaim.
next: If deal freshness ever matters at sub-5-minute scale, wire the cache invalidation to a projection-DB mtime probe instead of the TTL (small change in src/server/handlers/public.js).
Collector breadth lanes are network-bound (retailer pacing), not CPU-bound - out of scope by design.
If a no-build asset pipeline ever lands, add content-hashed filenames so static assets can go immutable.
Re-run the harness after each nightly archive growth: node tools/bench-server.js --reps 30 and node tools/bench-archive.js
